description: Behind a slope of broken bedsteads you find a Rust Rat nest, lined with black Umbrella Silk, and in it, folded into the walls with real care, most of Sprocket Row: the pram wheel, the bicycle bells, a run of brass door numbers that spell nothing, and a great many spoons, crested, none of them the Row's. The Rats have arranged it all by size. The nest is empty. Its builders, by the sound of the heaps, are not far.

options.label: Carry all of it home, spoons included, and hand it to the Row. The Row will feed you for it.

success.text: It takes two trips and everything your back has. The Row receives its property back in a silence that turns, by the pie shop, into something like applause. The pram wheel goes back on the pram. The door numbers go back on the wrong doors, and stay there, because by now everyone has got used to them. The spoons go in a drawer at the pie shop, nobody's, and the pie shop presses two Rations on you for the heaps.
success.note: Rust Rats line their nests with black Umbrella Silk and keep what they find, sorted by size, from Sprocket Row's pram wheels to crested spoons the Row never owned.

options.label: Carry home the Row's own things, and keep the crested spoons to sell. The Row owes you nothing then.

success.text: The Row gets its wheel, its bells and its numbers. The spoons you keep, on the principle that nobody on Sprocket Row ever owned a crested spoon and so nobody on Sprocket Row will miss one. They were thrown out from somewhere a good deal higher up the city, and the Rats kept them better than their owners did.
